checked.claim: soxr.ResampleStream is the best streaming resampler: about 2.8 µs per 10 ms block versus 15.7 µs for samplerate and 46 µs for resample_poly, with variable output sizes such as 0, 186, 166.
checked.evidence: soxr is the cheapest. My re-run on a loaded machine gave soxr HQ 12.2 µs per block, samplerate sinc_fastest 55.5 µs and resample_poly 238 µs, and all of these are negligible against a 10 ms budget. What the comparison misses is buffering latency. With 480-sample input blocks, soxr HQ emits output in bursts ([0,0,0,490,0,0,489,…]), not as 0/186/166. An impulse test gave about 30 ms end-to-end latency for soxr HQ, versus about 10 ms (one block) for soxr LQ, samplerate sinc_fastest and samplerate sinc_medium. HQ therefore adds about 20 ms (up to 37 ms backlog) of latency that the per-block microbenchmark does not show.
checked.correction: For a live tracker, pick the resampler on latency rather than µs. Use soxr quality='LQ'/'MQ', or samplerate.Resampler('sinc_fastest'/'sinc_medium'), or open the device at a rate the interface supports and resample offline only. If you keep soxr HQ, account for the extra 20–35 ms lag in the tracker.

recommendation_assessment:
Most of the recommendation holds up. uv with Python 3.12, torch 2.14.1 plus the forward-compatible torchaudio 2.11.0 and torchcodec 0.17, and sounddevice for capture are all sound. So is the split of MPS for offline work and CPU for the per-hop real-time path. The three packaging fixes are real, and upstream bugs corroborate two of them:
- samplerate 0.1.0's x86_64 dylib (issue #293)
- the undeclared audioread (issue #310)
- the PyPI ctc-forced-aligner name clash

Five changes are needed.

(1) **librosa 1.0 vs synctoolbox (biggest miss).** The reference repo imports synctoolbox at runtime (backend/app/core/utils.py: sync_via_mrmsdtw, DLNCO features) and libfmp (evaluation.py). synctoolbox 1.4.2 requires librosa<1.0, numba<0.66 and numpy<2.5. Resolving `librosa>=1.0` together with synctoolbox fails: "your requirements are unsatisfiable". With synctoolbox included, uv resolves librosa 0.11.0, numba 0.65.1 and numpy 2.4.6 while keeping torch 2.14.1 and audio-separator 0.47.0. librosa 1.0 also removed `get_duration(filename=)`, which the reference repo's online_dtw.py and stream_processor.py call (TypeError verified). Choose one:
- pin librosa 0.11, numpy<2.5 and numba<0.66 (simplest if reusing reference code and MrMsDTW; audioread then comes back through librosa)
- keep librosa 1.0 and either port the few synctoolbox functions or relax its pins with override-dependencies (untested)

(2) **Transcode inputs to WAV first.** librosa 1.0 loads only through soundfile, and audio-separator passes file paths straight to librosa.load. AAC .m4a originals, common for purchased music, fail with "Format not recognised" (verified), and installing audioread does not help. Make the first prep step transcode every input once with ffmpeg to WAV/FLAC. Use that single canonical file for separation, alignment and reference features; this also avoids AAC priming offsets differing between decoders (an AAC encoder-delay effect, not separately measured). Alternatively, decode with torchaudio/torchcodec and pass the ndarray to Separator.

(3) **onnx-weekly lock pin.** The lock pins onnx-weekly 1.24.0.dev20261012, a nightly. The ONNX release docs say weekly builds for a version may be deleted after its stable release, so the lock can become unrestorable once onnx 1.24 ships. Stable onnx is currently 1.23.2. `[tool.uv] exclude-dependencies = ["onnx-weekly"]` plus `onnx>=1.23` locks cleanly on uv 0.13 (verified); onnx2torch at runtime with stable onnx was not tested. Otherwise, keep a wheelhouse.

(4) **Resampler criterion.** Choose the streaming resampler on latency, not µs. soxr HQ adds about 20 ms (up to about 37 ms) of buffering with 10 ms blocks. soxr LQ/MQ or samplerate sinc_fastest stay at about one block.

(5) **Correct the version-floor rationale.** The downgrades to torch 2.11 / audio-separator 0.45 come from `uv pip compile`'s default macOS 13 target, not from uv's resolver. `uv lock` picks the latest versions even on Python 3.11, so 3.11 is not 'out' for torch.

Minor additions: set AUDIO_SEPARATOR_MODEL_DIR, which audio-separator honors, for a persistent model cache. The reference CRNN checkpoints are trained on TIMIT (English, 39 phonemes), so the phoneme-feature track should not assume they transfer to Korean or Japanese singing.
missed_options: Pin librosa 0.11.0, numpy 2.4.x and numba 0.65.x so synctoolbox 1.4.2 and libfmp (MrMsDTW, DLNCO features used by the reference repo) stay installable. This also restores audioread-based loading of m4a/AAC. Verified to resolve with torch 2.14.1 and audio-separator 0.47.0 on Python 3.12.
Keep librosa 1.0 but relax synctoolbox's pins (librosa<1.0, numba<0.66, numpy<2.5) with [tool.uv] override-dependencies, or vendor the few synctoolbox functions needed. Untested at runtime.

Replace onnx-weekly with stable onnx via `[tool.uv] exclude-dependencies = ["onnx-weekly"]` plus `onnx>=1.23`. Verified that it locks on uv 0.13; onnx2torch runtime with stable onnx is untested. Alternatively, archive the wheels in a local wheelhouse so the lock stays reproducible after weekly builds are deleted.

Make transcoding to WAV/FLAC with ffmpeg the first prep step and use one canonical file everywhere, or decode with torchaudio/torchcodec (which handles m4a through Homebrew FFmpeg) and pass the ndarray to audio_separator's Separator.
Use the AUDIO_SEPARATOR_MODEL_DIR environment variable, which audio-separator 0.47 supports, for a persistent offline model cache instead of /tmp.

Use low-latency streaming resampling: soxr quality='LQ'/'MQ' or samplerate.Resampler('sinc_fastest'/'sinc_medium'). Both measured at about 10 ms end to end with 10 ms blocks, versus about 30 ms for soxr HQ.

When exporting requirements with uv pip compile, set MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0 (torch 2.14 and onnxruntime 1.31 publish only macosx_14_0 wheels) rather than relying on floors to dodge the macOS 13 default target.

Python 3.11 is a viable fallback: uv lock gives torch 2.14.1, audio-separator 0.47.0 and onnxruntime 1.31.0, losing only numpy 2.5, scipy 1.18 and librosa 1.0. It also pairs naturally with the synctoolbox-compatible librosa 0.11 track.
Apple-Silicon-native MLX separation ports (demucs-mlx 1.6.1, mlx-audio 0.5.8 on PyPI, both MIT) as a possibly faster offline alternative to torch MPS. Quality and speed were not verified.
demucs 4.1.0 is now maintained at adefossez/demucs (facebookresearch/demucs is archived) and avoids diffq, samplerate and audioread entirely. Note its lameenc dependency is LGPL-3.0.
